name: Massachusetts
summary: Massachusetts is one of the strongest US markets for BTM C&I storage because several large value streams line up on summer weekday afternoons. ConnectedSolutions Daily Dispatch pays up to $200/kW-summer (5-yr rate lock, 30-60 day-ahead ~3-h events), with Winter Dispatch adding $25/kW. Peak-window demand charges are high: about $10.48/kW for NGrid G-3, and roughly $30-35/kW-month of distribution plus transmission demand on Eversource Greater Boston G-2/G-3. NGrid G-3 customers can elect a transmission coincident-peak charge (~$21.91/kW-month at the ISO-NE monthly peak hour). Capacity tags are worth ~$31/kW-yr (FCA 17) rising to ~$43/kW-yr (FCA 18), but only through pass-through supply contracts, and the 2028+ prompt-auction price is unknown. Key risks: CPS price softening after the May 2026 minimum-standard cut, no upfront C&I storage incentive, Expedited/Standard interconnection for anything above 25 kW (and network service in Boston), and NFPA 855-2020 limits (600 kWh per indoor fire area) that push larger units outdoors.

utilities.name: National Grid (Massachusetts Electric Company)
utilities.load_zone: Mostly WCMA; also parts of NEMA (North Shore/Merrimack Valley) and SEMA (zone mapping from general knowledge, not re-verified). FCA 17/18 cleared at a single price in all zones, so zone does not change capacity value for 2026/27-2027/28.
utilities.default_supply_notes: Basic Service: large C&I (G-3) priced monthly (varying monthly fixed $/kWh, procured via wholesale RFPs); small/medium C&I on fixed multi-month prices. Capacity and transmission costs embedded in Basic Service $/kWh, so ICAP tag reductions have no direct value on Basic Service (structure from general knowledge; confirm in current Basic Service filings).
utilities.network_grid_notes: Secondary spot/area networks exist in some downtown areas (e.g., Worcester, Lowell, Brockton-type urban cores; locations not verified). Network-served BESS face Simplified limits of < 1/15 of minimum load (area network also <=15 kW) and network-protector reverse-power constraints; plan on non-export and Standard review.

interconnection.rule_name: Standards for Interconnection of Distributed Generation (statewide DPU-approved DG Interconnection Tariff; National Grid M.D.P.U. No. 1579 eff. 2025-04-15; Eversource M.D.P.U. No. 55; Unitil Schedule IC)

tracks.name: Simplified
tracks.conditions: Listed (UL 1741) inverter-based facility on a radial EPS: <=15 kW single-phase or <=25 kW three-phase (subject to service configuration and aggregate-on-transformer conditions). On a spot network: rating < 1/15 of the customer's minimum load. On an area network: < 1/15 of minimum load AND <=15 kW. The 15->25 kW three-phase threshold was a TSRG consensus revision reflected in the 2025 tariff.

tracks.name: Expedited
tracks.conditions: Listed facilities on a radial EPS that pass the tariff's pre-specified screens (no single kW cap; screens on feeder/section penetration, transformer loading, etc.). Facilities with zero Export Capacity (non-exporting) skip the export-related screen. TSRG consensus also proposed a Group Study exemption for certain Expedited facilities.

tracks.name: Standard
tracks.conditions: All facilities that do not qualify for or fail Simplified/Expedited, including most facilities on secondary networks above the Simplified network limits; full impact/facilities studies; may be placed in a group study.

interconnection.non_export_path: Tariff defines Export Capacity as nameplate or a lower amount if limited by an acceptable means (e.g., PCS / UL 1741 CRD power control, reverse/minimum-power relays). Non-exporting systems (zero Export Capacity) skip the export screen in Expedited; storage is evaluated on export capacity rather than nameplate where controls are accepted. Exact list of acceptable export-limiting means and inadvertent-export allowances not verified in this pass.
interconnection.storage_specific_notes: Energy storage definitions were updated in the Simplified/Expedited redlines (TSRG / D.P.U. 25-29 proceeding). A 30 kW three-phase battery exceeds the 25 kW Simplified limit (Expedited at minimum). For network-served sites, Simplified is effectively limited to tiny systems (< 1/15 of minimum load); expect Standard review and strict non-export.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: ISO-NE capacity tag (peak load contribution): customer's metered load in the single hour of the ISO-NE annual system peak; the tag is applied to the customer's supply for the following year (EDCs reset tags annually; Jan-1 reset convention assumed, not re-verified).
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: Next controllable tag-setting peak is summer 2027 (summer 2026 peak has passed). Proxy price = FCA 18 clearing price for 2027/28 = $3.580/kW-month x 12 = $42.96/kW-yr. For comparison, current 2026/27 (FCA 17) = $2.590 x 12 = $31.08/kW-yr. A tag applied Jan-Dec 2028 would span Jan-May 2028 at $3.580 and Jun-Dec 2028 at the (unknown) first prompt-auction price for 2028/29. Excludes ISO-NE capacity-load-obligation scaling (CSO vs. sum of peak contributions), losses and supplier margin - gross-up factor not verified, so 1.0 used.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: Supply-side only. Realized only if the competitive supply contract passes capacity through at the customer's tag (index/pass-through product). On utility Basic Service or a fixed all-in contract the saving accrues to the supplier, not the customer (until contract renewal re-prices the tag).

tariffs.storage_notes: No demand charge, so BTM storage value on G-1 is limited to ConnectedSolutions, ICAP tag (if supply passes through) and CPS. Sites this small rarely justify even the 30 kW/150 kWh unit unless resilience-driven.

On utility Basic Service or a fixed all-in contract the saving accrues to the supplier, not the customer (until contract renewal re-prices the tag).

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: OPTIONAL for G-3 (elected; D.P.U. 23-150, available since April 2025): customer's coincident 60-minute kW at the hour of the ISO-NE Regional Network Service monthly transmission system peak, billed every month, replacing the volumetric transmission charge.
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: $21.91/kW-month x 12 months = $262.92 per kW reduced at every monthly peak hour (theoretical maximum; requires hitting all 12 monthly RNS peak hours). A second search summary showed $23.82/kW (likely a different month's rate) - confirm current value in the latest M.D.P.U. 1-26-x summary. Net benefit vs. default = avoided volumetric transmission $/kWh minus CP charge on remaining coincident kW.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: Delivery (utility) charge - realized on the utility bill regardless of competitive supplier. Election appears to carry a minimum term (Eversource analogue: 12 months) - verify NGrid election rules. Gross value: electing the option replaces volumetric transmission charges, so the net benefit is volumetric cost avoided minus the CP charge on the remaining CP kW. Catching all 12 monthly peaks is demanding.

tariffs.storage_notes: Customer charge $350/month. Demand window (8am-9pm weekdays, all months) is 13 h long - a 2-3 h battery can only shave short/peaky profiles; flat daytime loads need long-duration (5 h) units. kVA basis (90% of kVA) means a PF-correcting inverter can also cut billed demand. The optional transmission CP charge is the single largest BTM lever on G-3 and aligns with ConnectedSolutions/ICAP hours in summer; winter monthly peaks are typically early evening (verify against ISO-NE history).

programs.administrator: Mass Save Program Administrators (National Grid, Eversource, Unitil, Cape Light Compact) - Active Demand Reduction initiative, 2025-2027 Plan

valuation.kw_basis: Average kW reduction delivered across ALL called event hours of the season (missed/under-performed hours count against the average)
valuation.cap: Exporting sites: performance capped at 150% of site annual peak load.
valuation.notes: 'Up to $200/kW-summer' per National Grid MA Daily Dispatch page (2026). Rate locked for the first 5 consecutive enrolled years for new battery systems. Residential battery rate is different ($275/kW) - do not confuse. Example: 65 kW/200 kWh sustaining 65 kW for 3 h -> 65 x $200 = $13,000/season if perfect; 200 kW/418 kWh can only hold ~139 kW for 3 h (418/3) -> ~$27,900/season.

dispatch.window: Events between 2pm and 7pm, starting/ending on the hour (2023 offering materials; confirm 2026 window)
dispatch.baseline_or_mv: Interval-meter based: average kW reduction (battery discharge net of baseline) over all event hours in the season

stacking.notes: Event hours (2-7pm summer weekdays) usually overlap the ISO-NE annual peak and monthly RNS peaks, so DD dispatch also cuts the ICAP tag and transmission CP. Conflicts: 30-60 events of ~3 h each can leave the battery depleted for a later in-window demand peak (NGrid G-3 window runs to 9pm). Conflicts as researched: ma-connectedsolutions-ci-targeted (cannot enroll same kW in both summer options); isone-adcr-aggregator (dual participation of same kW generally not allowed - verify)

programs.vpp_relevance: Core MA VPP revenue: PAs dispatch day-ahead to fleets; a single CSP/aggregator can enroll multiple sites, which is the natural on-ramp to a multi-site VPP.

panel_notes.note: The G-3 transmission CP election (~$21.91/kW-month at the ISO-NE monthly RNS peak) is worth more per kW than distribution demand; but it is all-or-nothing each month, so a missed peak hour can erase the savings versus the volumetric default. Model the election with real ISO-NE peak-hour history before opting in.

G-3 bills the max 15-min demand in the 8am-9pm weekday window or 90% of kVA, so a 2-h battery rarely flattens a 13-h window on flat loads. Use inverter reactive support for PF-driven sites; and charge nights/weekends, which carry no billed demand.

Daily Dispatch pays on average kW across every event hour of the season - one empty battery on a 3-h event drags the season average. Reserve SOC for the 2-7pm events before chasing late-afternoon demand peaks.

panel_notes.topic: Pick the right legacy-area rate sheet
panel_notes.note: Eversource still publishes separate rate summaries for Greater Boston, Cambridge, South Shore/Cape/MV and Western MA, and G-2/G-3 thresholds and charges differ by area. Pull the site's own summary; the Greater Boston G-2 150-300 kW tier carries ~$19.39 distribution + $15.20 transmission per kW.
Downtown Boston and Cambridge sites on spot/area networks will not pass Simplified (< 1/15 of minimum load). Plan on Standard review with strict non-export and network-protector coordination.

ICAP tag value (~$31/kW-yr at FCA 17, ~$43/kW-yr at FCA 18) only reaches the customer on a pass-through/index supply contract, not on Basic Service or a fixed all-in price. Align contract renewals so the reduced tag is priced in, and note the 2028/29 prompt-auction price is unknown.

In MA the ConnectedSolutions summer events, the ISO-NE annual peak (ICAP), summer RNS monthly peaks and CPS summer windows mostly line up in weekday late afternoons, so one dispatch strategy captures all four. ConnectedSolutions (~$200/kW-summer) dwarfs wholesale capacity (~$2.6-3.6/kW-month), so keep ADCR as optional upside.
The May 2026 emergency cut to the 2026-2030 CPS minimum standard and shorter banking make CPEC prices more surplus-sensitive. Underwrite well below the $65 ACP and treat CPS as upside for BTM C&I.

Against 3-h Daily Dispatch events, the 200 kW/418 kWh unit delivers only ~139 kW average (418/3), while 65 kW/200 kWh (3.1 h) and 200 kW/600 kWh (3.0 h) hold full power. Size enrolled kW to usable kWh/3 after reserve and round-trip losses.

Every product exceeds the 25 kW Simplified cap, so file Expedited as non-exporting (UL 1741 PCS/CRD export control) to skip export screens. Watch the 150%-of-peak ConnectedSolutions cap if you plan any export.

Under 527 CMR 1.00 Ch. 52 / NFPA 855-2020, indoor Li-ion is capped at 600 kWh per fire area, and >50 kWh units need UL 9540A large-scale test acceptance. For 418/600 kWh units, default to outdoor pads with 10 ft clearances, and confirm whether the 2024 527 CMR edition is in force at permitting.
